Your digital thread work at ARV is exactly the L3–L4 integration story: Teamcenter as system of record for EBOM/MBOM/change; Plex for routing, as-built, quality, inventory; T4EA as the integration layer; Power BI dashboards for manufacturing and supply chain. Say it in those terms.

cards.f: Use cases with the metric each moves
cards.b:
• Predictive quality / real-time SPC — scrap rate, first-pass yield. (Design D7)
  • Predictive maintenance — unplanned downtime, MTBF; needs historian data plus maintenance records; start with the two assets with the worst downtime.
  • Warranty analytics — warranty cost per unit, time-to-detect field issues. (Design D10)
  • Supply chain visibility and inventory optimization — OTD, days of inventory, working capital. (Design D13)
  • Energy analytics — kWh per unit; submetering + production schedule + tariff data; shift heavy loads to cheaper windows.
  • Engineering acceleration — RAG over engineering docs and change history; simulation data management; design reuse via the digital thread.
  • OEM requirements — Ford/GM/Stellantis impose PPAP, APQP, IATF 16949 traceability, EDI, and increasingly data-sharing for sustainability (carbon per part) and Catena-X-style exchange. Traceability requirements shape genealogy data design.
If you could do one AI use case in year one?

Predictive quality on the highest-scrap line, because the data already exists in the MES and historian, the metric is unambiguous, the payback is in months, and it forces the foundation — sensor-to-MES joins, genealogy, quality labels — that every later use case reuses. Warranty analytics is the close second because the dollars are larger, but the data is messier and the loop is slower.

Industry 4.0 in one breath

Connected assets, contextualized data (ISA-95 joins), and closed-loop decisions — from descriptive dashboards to predictive and prescriptive actions on the floor. Data and AI enable it by making plant data trustworthy and available in minutes rather than months, then putting models where operators act.
cards.s: 5.3 Manufacturing domain — the vocabulary and the use cases

cards.b: IATF 16949, ISO 9001, PPAP/APQP/FMEA, ISA-95/ISA-88, OPC-UA, ISO 27001 and TISAX for information security, GDPR for EU plants and employees, NIST CSF, and where relevant CMMC. Sustainability reporting (CSRD, product carbon footprint) is arriving as a data requirement from OEMs.
cards.s: 5.3 Manufacturing domain — the vocabulary and the use cases

cards.b:
• Lifecycle: problem framing with a metric → data readiness → baseline → model → offline eval → shadow/canary → monitoring (drift, performance, business metric) → retraining cadence.
  • Tooling: feature store, experiment tracking and model registry (MLflow, SageMaker), pipelines (SageMaker Pipelines, Vertex, Airflow), serving (batch first; real-time only where latency matters), monitoring (Evidently, SageMaker Model Monitor).
  • GenAI: RAG grounded in governed documents; evaluation sets before rollout; guardrails on input and output; cost per query; on-prem or VPC-isolated models for IP-sensitive engineering data — you've done this.
  • Agentic AI: tool-calling loops with human approval on side-effecting actions, audit trails (your flight recorder), and scoped permissions. Be the person in the room who has shipped one.
  • Responsible AI: model cards, bias and safety review proportional to impact, a policy for what may leave the enterprise boundary.

decks.title: Industry use cases to cite
decks.blurb: Manufacturing, automotive, IoT, retail, finance examples.

cards.b:
• Predictive maintenance — Bosch / Siemens plants: vibration and current signatures from motors and spindles (historian, 1-s cadence) → Isolation Forest and gradient boosting on rolling features → work orders raised days before failure. Metric: unplanned downtime hours, maintenance cost. Pitfall: few labeled failures; start unsupervised.
  • Visual inspection — BMW paint shop, Foxconn boards: camera images → CNN (ResNet/EfficientNet, often transfer-learned from a few hundred defect images, augmented) → flag and divert. Metric: escape rate, inspector hours. Pitfall: lighting and camera drift; retrain per line.
  • Predictive quality / virtual metrology — semiconductor fabs, machining: process parameters during the cycle predict the measurement result before metrology; skip or prioritize inspection. Metric: first-pass yield, inspection cost.
  • Digital twin — GE turbines, Siemens Amberg: a physics-plus-data model of an asset updated by telemetry; simulate what-if before touching the real thing. Your Cameo–Volta–GT-SUITE integration is a design-side digital twin.
  • Warranty early warning — every OEM and Tier 1: claims by build cohort with Weibull curves; NLP on claim text; trace to supplier lot. Metric: warranty cost per unit, weeks to detect. Example: a Tier 1 catching a seal supplier's lot change six weeks earlier saves a field campaign.
  • OEE and downtime analytics — any plant: MES downtime codes + historian → Pareto of loss reasons → targeted fixes. The unglamorous project with the fastest payback; often the first data product.
  • Energy optimization — steel and foundries: submetering + production schedule + tariff → shift heavy loads, detect leaks. Metric: kWh per unit, demand charges.
  • Supply-chain control tower — Ford, Schneider Electric: ERP + supplier EDI + logistics feeds → exception alerts and inventory optimization (MIP with ML-forecast demand). Metric: on-time delivery, days of inventory, expedite spend.
  • Generative AI on the floor — Siemens Industrial Copilot, Schaeffler: RAG over manuals, work instructions, and maintenance logs; operators ask in natural language. Metric: time to resolve, onboarding time for new technicians.
  • Traceability and OEM data demands: Catena-X (European automotive data space) for part passports and carbon footprint per part; IATF-driven genealogy. The data platform has to answer "which vehicles got parts from lot X" in minutes.

• Fleet health — Tesla, Rivian, iRobot, Peloton: telemetry by firmware × hardware rev dashboards; OTA rollouts gated on fleet metrics; anomaly detection per device vs fleet baseline. Metric: field failure rate, support contacts per 1,000 devices.
  • Usage-based services — Whisker health insights, Oura, Fitbit: sessionized events → per-user baselines → change-point detection → notifications with explanations. Metric: engagement, subscription conversion, false-alert rate (high false alerts kill trust).
  • Replenishment — Amazon Dash, HP Instant Ink, printer consumables: usage telemetry predicts consumable depletion → auto-reorder. Directly applicable to litter subscriptions.
  • Usage-based insurance — your Stellantis UBI work; Progressive Snapshot: driving telemetry → risk scoring (gradient boosting on trip features) → pricing. Privacy and consent are the hard part.
  • Smart home — Nest, Ecobee: schedule learning (clustering + simple models) and demand-response programs with utilities.

• Digital engineering / MBSE — Army XM30, Air Force digital acquisition: SysML models as the authoritative source; digital thread from requirements to as-built; simulation-based verification. Your day job.
  • Predictive maintenance for fleets — USAF Condition-Based Maintenance Plus: aircraft sensor data → component remaining useful life (survival models, LSTMs) → depot scheduling. Metric: mission-capable rate.
  • Secure AI — on-prem LLMs for CUI/classified: air-gapped model hosting, retrieval ACLs, log anonymization (your Presidio scoping). The constraint that produced your architecture is now an industry pattern.

• Retail — Walmart, Target: demand forecasting (gradient boosting, DeepAR) per store-SKU; markdown optimization; recommendation systems (collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, two-tower neural models).
  • Finance — banks, Stripe: fraud detection (gradient boosting + graph features + real-time streaming with sub-100 ms scoring); credit risk (logistic regression for explainability); anti-money-laundering (graph analytics).
  • Healthcare — Mayo, Kaiser: readmission risk, sepsis early warning (time-series models on vitals), imaging (CNNs); heavy governance (HIPAA, FDA SaMD for models that are medical devices).
  • Energy and utilities — your grid-monitoring platform; National Grid: load forecasting, outage prediction from weather and asset age, smart-meter analytics; streaming ingestion from heterogeneous field devices.
  • Logistics — UPS ORION, Maersk: route optimization (OR), ETA prediction (ML), container tracking (IoT).
  • Telecom — Verizon, Ericsson: network anomaly detection, churn prediction, capacity planning — the origin of much AIOps practice.

cards.f: How to use these in an answer
cards.b: Name the pattern, then the specific: "This is the same shape as predictive maintenance in a Bosch plant — vibration features, unsupervised first because failures are rare, then a supervised model once you have labels. For your line I'd start with the two assets with the worst downtime." One sentence of analogy, one sentence of how you'd apply it here.
